Yes, in this snapshot `Path` exposes `move_into`, and it was added in Python 3.14.

The documentation in `library/pathlib.rst` describes `Path.move_into(target_dir)`. It moves a file or directory tree into an existing directory and returns a new `Path` pointing to the moved path. It carries a `.. versionadded:: 3.14` note.

```json
{"facts": {"available": "true", "added": "3.14"}}
```
